method: Independent semantic review against each concept's prerequisites, required facts and blocked_future_concepts. Exhaustive review of lesson titles, text/visual/code blocks, media summaries and bridges, recap, up-next and remediation text. Sampled 4 of 9 interactions across all three tiles, including choice prompts/options/feedback and code prompts/workspaces/hints. No deterministic gates re-run; no prior evaluator reports or generator reasoning consulted.

findings_summary: Application-lifespan teaching uses its own acquisition/yield/cleanup/registration facts and prerequisite Python/ASGI concepts. SharedClient is a local stand-in; understanding outbound HTTP, dependency injection, routing or production shutdown verification is unnecessary. The observation harness is explicitly unchanged scaffolding.

ORM teaching stays within stored foreign-key association, object navigation and reciprocal back_populates, supported by prior entity mapping. References to later loading/query behavior are boundary cautions, not instruction that requires understanding those later topics.

Field-constraint teaching does not require nested models. Nested-model teaching begins separately at tile_020.s07 and remains within composition and nested error locations, without requiring request-body binding, HTTP validation-error handling or domain validators. The recap combines already-taught concepts in separately attributed blocks.

Up-next previews name later topics without requiring their understanding. Registered workspaces isolate ORM and validation examples; shared scenario vocabulary does not introduce a later-concept dependency.
limitations: Interaction conclusions cover the declared sample rather than an exhaustive interaction audit. Media review covers packaged summaries and bridge text; external video playback was not available.
